packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-09 - unverified first reading from images only

Exposure / method notes
- No identification of the work or author was revealed to me. Modern pencil labels on the parchment read approximately "Stams, StA, Fg. 71r" (face 1) and "Stams, StA, Fg. 71v" (face 2). Face 1 also carries "Aus VIII/25" and "anno 1616" (a binding or reuse note). The directory name contains "stams". I did not use any of these to identify the text.
- Beyond the rules: I made enlarged crops of image-002, image-003 and image-005 in my own scratch directory, plus greyscale contrast-equalized versions of the same regions to bring up faded ink. I viewed only those derived crops and the 14 packet images.
- All 14 images loaded.

Layout survey (observations)
- image-001 = overview of face 1, with native tiles image-002 (upper left), image-003 (upper right), image-004 (middle left), image-005 (middle right), image-006 (lower left) and image-007 (lower right). image-008 = overview of face 2, with tiles image-009 to image-014 in the same arrangement. The tiles overlap.
- A leaf about 21 x 31 cm, two columns, written in a small, heavily abbreviated Gothic textualis or notula-type book hand. There are many red paragraph marks (C-shaped capitula signs with long red hairline extensions into the intercolumn). There are red rubric headings and large red initials (O / Q types with long tails). A horizontal fold runs across the middle, and there are diagonal creases.
- The ink is very abraded and faded, especially on face 1 col. a and the lower half of both faces. Face 2 is somewhat clearer in col. a.
- Red rubric headings visible:
  * Face 1, col. b (image-005 l.~20 / image-001 middle): "De tranquillitate? / De translacione? ..." followed by a large red initial Q? or O with a tail. The rubric is badly rubbed.
  * Face 1, lower col. b (image-007, near the bottom): a red line, perhaps "De [..]... apud? [..]" (illegible).
  * Face 2, intercolumn of col. a (image-010): "De / renu(n)cia / tione R(ubrica)" written in red in three short lines, with a large red initial A (with an "O" above it, perhaps a guide letter or a two-part initial) in the left margin of col. a.
  * Face 2, col. b (image-012): a red guide letter "D" above the rubric, then the red rubric "De suplenda negligencia prelat[orum]", followed by a large red initial O/Q with a long descending tail.
  * Face 2, col. b lower (image-014): the red rubric "De t(em)p(or)ib(us) ordinacionu(m) (et) qualitate ordina[ndorum]" (read: "D(e) t(em)pib(us) ordiacon(um) (et) [q]ualitate (et) qli(tate) ordi..."; the letters are uncertain after "ordiaco(n)u(m)"), followed by a large red initial Q.
  * Face 2, left margin of col. a (image-013): marginal notes in brown ink in a smaller hand: "In? ca? mapl?..." / "..m pesse? / ..nonun..(?) / ..de?..". Illegible.
- Tentative interpretation: a sequence of short paragraphs, each opened by a red paragraph sign, under titled sections ("De renunciatione", "De supplenda negligentia prelatorum", "De temporibus ordinationum et qualitate ordinandorum"). It looks like a systematic treatise or a summary arranged under titles. I am not identifying it.

Selected spans
- Face 1, col. b, upper (image-003, contrast-enhanced): about 18 lines, read as far as possible.
- Face 1, col. b, beginnings of lines (image-002, right part).
- Face 2: the rubrics (above), plus the clearer col. a lines at the top (image-009) and in the middle (image-011, image-013).
- Unread: almost all of face 1 col. a (very abraded), the lower thirds of both faces, and most of face 2 col. b. These need multispectral or UV imaging. Normal light will not recover them.

Conventions: [..] marks lost or illegible text, and "?" marks an uncertain reading. Many words are given only as letter-strings with abbreviation marks, because the expansion is not secure.

Limitations
- This is a very low-yield reading. The ink is rubbed down to a ghost on most of the leaf. Only the rubrics, some letter clusters, and a handful of short words ("possit elegi", "Si quis", "et", "q(uo)d") are reasonably secure.
- Many of the expansions above are guesses at the shape of an abbreviation, not readings. Weight the rubric texts much more heavily than the body lines.
- Column order: I read face 1 col. b and face 2 col. a only partially, and face 1 col. a and face 2 col. b hardly at all.
- Multispectral or UV imaging of the whole leaf is the next step. Normal-light crops at higher magnification were not enough, even with contrast enhancement.
